feladatok.cim: Email to Chris accepting an astronomy evening
feladatok.helyzet: You are spending two months in London and your friend Chris has sent you an email inviting you to the following programme on Saturday night:

bemenet.cim: An Evening with the Stars at Royal Observatory Greenwich
bekezdesek: Come to the Royal Observatory Greenwich for a night of astronomy. The programme consists of a planetarium show to illustrate what’s in the night sky on the day of your visit, a chance to look through our gigantic 18-tonne Victorian telescope, and some time on the Prime Meridian after dark with an amazing view, a hot drink and astronomers to answer your questions.

feladatok.teendo: Write an email of 50-80 words to Chris in which you
iranyito_szempontok: choose the time you prefer and say why.

feladatok.cim: Reply to Peter about pressure from a talented family
feladatok.helyzet: You read the following post on an internet forum for teenagers’ problems:

bekezdesek: My family are all extremely talented and I just know I’m going to be the one who breaks the pattern.
I’m a 17-year-old boy and am in year 11 doing my A level examinations. I’m finding it so much harder than I ever imagined.

I have an older sister and an older brother and there’s always been a lot of rivalry. My brother is 25 and did brilliantly at everything. He’s now a lawyer. My sister is 19. She got into the national swimming team last year and still got fantastic A levels. She’s at Cambridge University now and everyone is so proud of her.

I know I’ll never achieve anything like that. Whatever I do, it’s never going to be as good as my sister and my brother. I know I’m the one putting pressure on myself but I get really panicky when I think about it. I feel like I’m going to be a big disappointment to my parents.

feladatok.teendo: Write a reply of 100-120 words to Peter in which you tell him
iranyito_szempontok: what you think about his problem,
if he should discuss it with his family,
what he could do to feel better.
